suite.description: State-machine and durable-operation fixtures of multi-device identity (IDENTITY-PROFILE-01 §12.3; LFCP-WIRE-01 §107).

conventions.steps: inputs.steps are performed in order; expected.steps gives each step's outcome and the facts it asserts.
conventions.references: A step case `wire:<id>` names a case of LFCP-IDENTITY-TEST-VECTORS-01, `profile:<id>` one of IDENTITY-PROFILE-TEST-VECTORS-01; the step outcome equals that case's expected outcome. `bytes_of` names a case whose exact bytes a step sends in another context, with the outcome the step states.
conventions.history: inputs.mode `sequence`: the steps of each Resource and `branch` form one history; the Control state a step's case is decided on contains the last record an earlier step of the same branch committed. An `aside` step shows a rule on another head and is not part of the history. Mode `independent`: each step stands alone.
conventions.phases: expected `phase` is the state of IDENTITY-PROFILE-01 §9.2 on the Control state of the step's case (`phase_input`), first match wins.
conventions.client_outcomes: Outcomes without a case are client-procedure results (phase states of IDENTITY-PROFILE-01 §9.2, statuses of §6); they have no wire code.

cases.description: Register DEV_A, write, revoke it, accept an old-head unit, close the epoch, quarantine the unit beyond the frontier and rebuild

rule.text: Revocation without rotation leaves old-head units acceptable until the closing KEY_EPOCH; beyond its frontier they are STALE_DATA_EPOCH and replicas rebuild without them.

steps.action: replicas R1 and R2 accept the registration
DEV_A writes sequence 1 at I1
DEV_B self-registers and writes at I2
BRIDGE writes at I8
OWNER revokes DEV_A
R1 receives DEV_A sequence 2 at the old head I1, latest I9, and merges it
OWNER closes epoch 0
R2 receives the same unit after K1
R1 learns K1 and rebuilds without DEV_A sequence 2

assertions: R1, which merged the unit before the revocation closed the epoch, and R2, which saw it only after, end with the same accepted set (LFCP-WIRE-01 §19.1).

cases.description: Revoking DEV_A suspends DEV_B by the cascade; re-certification by the root makes it active again; DEV_B units at each head

rule.text: A suspended device is not revoked; the root or another managing device may re-certify it with a chain that avoids the revoked issuer.

steps.action: DEV_B self-registers with [CERT_B, CERT_A]
DEV_B writes at I2
OWNER revokes DEV_A
DEV_B writes at I9
DEV_B cannot re-certify itself
OWNER re-certifies DEV_B with [CERT_B2]
DEV_B writes at I10

assertions: The unit at I9 stays refused after I10: activity is evaluated at the head a unit references.

cases.description: Self-registration proposed on a stale head, re-evaluated on the new head; the same DEVICE_GRANT proposed twice

rule.text: A proposer that meets CONTROL_HEAD_MISMATCH synchronises and classifies its phase on the accepted chain; a repeated record is not a transition and the intent is complete.

steps.action: The coordinator holds I1
DEV_B proposes its self-registration on J2 (a stale head)
DEV_B synchronises: its register phase is pending on I1
DEV_B proposes a fresh record on I1
A second installation with the same intent classifies it on I2
Had it proposed a fresh DEVICE_GRANT with the same leaf, rule 5 refuses it (shown for DEV_A on I1)
The exact bytes of a committed record sent again

assertions: No record is proposed twice as a new transition; a re-sent exact record gets the same ACK.

cases.description: The owner revokes BOB's grant: every device of BOB is inactive; a re-grant restores them without new device records

rule.text: Revoking the root's standing silences all its devices; restoring it restores them without re-registration.

steps.action: OWNER revokes J1
DEV_C writes at I11
DEV_C opens X at I11
OWNER grants BOB again
DEV_C writes at I12

assertions: Activity returns with standing; no DEVICE_GRANT is needed.

cases.description: Reconciliation of X against I's Control state: revocations first, then registrations, then keys; idempotent; two reconcilers race

rule.text: Revocations first; registrations of personal devices active in I and not registered in X; keys by the ledger; a second run proposes nothing.

steps.action: I's state at P4: DEV_A and DEV_B registered, (OWNER, PAIR_J) consumed
X's state: DEV_B self-registered with [CERT_B, CERT_A], DEV_A bound only as an intermediate
Step 1: no revoked pair of I is relevant in X: the consume of PAIR_J, a pairing device not bound in X, is not propagated (IDENTITY-PROFILE-01 §7.1 step 1)
Step 2: DEV_A, bound only as an intermediate in X, is registered with I's chain; DEV_B has the same leaf certificate ID and needs nothing
Step 3: the reconciler seals every epoch of X it holds to DEV_A and DEV_B unless its ledger records the package
A second reconciler had proposed the same registration on the previous head: CONTROL_HEAD_MISMATCH; after synchronising its phase is
A second run of the reconciler
The Identity Resource as its own target: steps 1 and 2 are vacuous, step 3 seals I's epochs to DEV_B
A service device whose issuer I has revoked is never registered in X: the revocation reaches X first and X refuses the chain (shown at I9)

assertions: Registration and key delivery are reconciled independently; an equal leaf certificate ID says nothing about packages.

cases.description: 65 sessions closed in I, then a personal device revoked in I before its first registration in X: reconciliation propagates that revocation alone

rule.text: Only revocations relevant in X are propagated; a pairing device is never bound outside I, so its revocation takes none of the 64 unbound pairs of its root in X. A refused propagation is reported and retried; once the device is bound in X its revocation is never limited.

steps.action: 65 pairing devices created and cancelled in I, then a 66th session opened by PAIR_M
Phase 1 of the 66th session, for DEV_P
Phase 2: DEV_P registered in I
DEV_P is lost and revoked in I before any reconciliation has registered it in X
Reconciliation of X, step 1: the 66 revoked pairing devices of I are not relevant in X
Step 1: the revocation of DEV_P is propagated, an unbound tombstone of OWNER
DEV_P tries to register itself in X with its old chain [CERT_P, CERT_A]
Had the pairing devices been propagated, the 65th unbound tombstone of OWNER would be refused (shown on 64 tombstones)
X already holds 64 unbound revoked pairs of OWNER: the propagation of DEV_P is refused
The reconciler registers neither DEV_P nor a device whose chain passes through it, and seals nothing to them
DEV_P registers itself in X with its old chain
The next reconciliation of X proposes the revocation again, DEV_P now bound in X: never limited, exposing

steps.outcome: DEV_P treated as revoked in X

steps.rotation: the rotation policy of §8.4 closes the epoch

assertions: The pairing sessions of I cost nothing in X; the revocation of a personal device that X never registered is recorded there and refuses its old chain.
At the limit a refused revocation is reported and retried; the device that registers itself meanwhile is revoked by the next reconciliation (an exposing revocation).

cases.description: Reconciliation step 4 on I with a pairing session open and closed: entries for personal and service devices only, retired entries, no change on a second run

rule.text: Display entries are restored for devices of kind 0 and 1 bound in I and not revoked; a retired entry only gets revoked = true; nothing is written for a pairing device; a second run writes nothing.

steps.action: I at P2, PAIR_J's session open; the document holds the root's entry only: DEV_A's entry is written, none for PAIR_J
A second run at P2, the session still open
I at P3, PAIR_J's session consumed (closed)
I at P4: DEV_B registered, its entry never written (the approver crashed before §5.3 step 6 wrote it)
A second run at P4
Service variant: I at P3s, PAIR_J consumed for BRIDGE_O (the document as after the run at P2)
I at P4s: BRIDGE_O bound in I with kind 1, not registered
DEV_A revoked in I: its entry is retired and gets revoked = true; BRIDGE_O, suspended, keeps its entry
A second run after the revocation
BRIDGE_O re-certified by the root: its entry stays

assertions: A pairing device has no entry (§2.1): a step 4 that wrote one would write a kind-2 entry that §4 marks invalid, and write it again on every run.
Every second run writes no metadata change, with the session open or closed.

cases.description: OWNER and DEV_A revoke DEV_B on one head with different reasons: one record; the other phase is complete

rule.text: Revoked with any other reason, by anyone: complete; the operation continues with the rotation test.

steps.action: X at I2
DEV_A proposes DEVICE_REVOKE {OWNER, DEV_B, 2} on I2
OWNER's DEVICE_REVOKE {OWNER, DEV_B, 1} on I2 was committed first
DEV_A synchronises and classifies its revoke phase
A fresh proposal of the same intent would be refused
DEV_A continues with the rotation test of §8.1

assertions: A different reason recorded by another installation is complete, not superseded.

cases.description: An invitation accepted by a device of DAVE: the claim names the root, the device registers itself and keys its root

rule.text: The claimant is the root; the device self-registers, seals the DEKs it holds to its root and adds the Resource to the roster.

steps.action: OWNER invites INVITE
DEV_D, a device of DAVE, claims with claimant DAVE, signed by INVITE
DEV_D registers itself
DEV_D seals epoch 0 to DAVE
DAVE opens X and reads
DEV_D adds X to the roster of I
A device named as claimant would be refused (shown on I2)

assertions: The root is the member; its devices act for it.

cases.description: Pairing DEV_B through PAIR_L in an Identity Resource already rotated to epoch 1: keys of both epochs, request, phases 1 and 2, reuse and equivocation

rule.text: A pairing session yields at most one approved payload; nothing is signed for D_B before the consume is committed (N9).

steps.action: I at P1: DEV_A registered
The root's Data Unit with actor sequence 1 carries the initial change (epoch 0)
The root's Data Unit with actor sequence 2 carries the fill change (epoch 0)
I is rotated to epoch 1
DEV_A holds both DEKs and the root's unit 1, and creates PAIR_L
DEV_A seals the DEK of epoch 0 to PAIR_L
DEV_A seals the DEK of epoch 1 to PAIR_L
The link of PAIR_L is shown
B opens the root's units 1 and 2 with the DEK of epoch 0 and replays their changes: the document of §5.1 (a Snapshot is used only after unit 1)
A Snapshot whose initial change is not the root's unit 1 is not used
B writes its request as PAIR_L in epoch 1
The document admits the change the unit carries
A shows the fingerprint
Phase 1: consume with digest(CERT_B)
A second manager that approved another request of the session proposes its consume
A phase-2 record with another digest is refused
Phase 2
Lost ACK of phase 2: the exact bytes are re-sent
DEV_A seals the DEK of epoch 0 to DEV_B
DEV_A seals the DEK of epoch 1 to DEV_B

assertions: Before the link is shown A holds, verified, the root's unit 1 and the DEK of every epoch of I, and seals them all to the pairing device (§5.3 step 1).
One session: the link, the binding, the signer of every pairing unit and the pairing field of every request change name PAIR_L.

cases.description: One link, two installations: sequential reuse, and concurrent equivocation

rule.text: Two installations given one link write as PAIR_L: the second writes sequence 2, or both units are excluded as equivocation and A sees no request.

steps.action: The first installation writes PAIR_L sequence 1
Sequential reuse: the second installation sees it and writes sequence 2
Concurrent: the second installation also writes sequence 1

assertions: An equivocating pair is excluded with the changes depending on it (SHARED-OBJECTS-PROFILE-01 §14.1).

cases.description: OWNER at 31 live devices in I: the pairing device takes the 32nd place, the consume frees it, D_B is registered; at 32 no link

rule.text: Rule 8 counts live bindings; a revoked pairing device frees its place.

steps.action: 31 live devices of OWNER in I (DEV_A and LIMIT_OWNER_01..30)
At 32 live devices a further pairing device is refused: no link until a device is revoked
The consume of PAIR_M frees its place
DEV_B takes the 32nd place

cases.description: 40 sessions created and cancelled one after the other, then a session completes

rule.text: Revoked pairing devices free their places.

steps.action: 40 pairing devices created and cancelled in I
Phase 1 of the 41st session
Phase 2 completes

cases.description: Pairing the service device BRIDGE_O: approved with C0 = CERT_SO (digest d), bound in I, C0's issuer revoked, re-certified as C1 = CERT_SO_R; the candidates

rule.text: Only a certificate whose digest equals the approval proves the result; a candidate whose chain never carried that leaf is unproven; a timeout is never a decision.

steps.action: Phase 1 with digest(CERT_SO)
Phase 2: bind-only DEVICE_GRANT in I
BRIDGE_O cannot write in I
Every candidate is offline: B shows
C0's issuer DEV_A is revoked in I
The root re-certifies BRIDGE_O as C1 (same kind, mask and scope)
Candidate X where C0 was never accepted: reconciliation step 1 does not propagate the consume of PAIR_J, a pairing device not bound in X
… it propagates the revocation of DEV_A
… then step 2 registers C1
Candidate X where C0 was registered first (before I revoked DEV_A)
Reconciliation step 1 does not propagate the consume of PAIR_J, a pairing device not bound in X
… it propagates the revocation of DEV_A, which suspends BRIDGE_O
Step 2 re-certifies BRIDGE_O as C1: B takes C0 from the history as its result and uses C1
The root seals the DEK of X to BRIDGE_O; with the certificate and the DEK it is ready
Candidate X where another issuer registered C* (scope [X, Y], another digest)
B restarts: it resumes from its persisted candidates
A crashes after the bind-only DEVICE_GRANT was accepted, before its ACK was persisted

assertions: The first verified certificate decides: until B holds one, no candidate outcome is known; a candidate absent from the scope is not granted.

cases.description: Request validation and the feasibility check before anything is committed

rule.text: A preset whose complete future chain fails W §7.3 steps 1 and 4 and W §17.4 rules 4 to 6 and 8 is not offered.

steps.action: A valid request
A request written by another pairing device into this one
The descriptor changes between display and confirmation
A manager with a chain of three certificates: Full is not offered
A manager whose mask lacks 3 cannot issue Edit
An Edit device cannot issue at all
A service scope trimmed to nothing
The manager's own authority is re-checked after a head change

assertions: No consume is proposed for a preset that fails the check.

cases.description: DEV_E, issued by DEV_C, revokes DEV_C: it re-certifies first, then revokes, then retires

rule.text: The revoker's own chain MUST NOT pass through D; it first obtains a fresh chain from the root or a managing device whose chain avoids D, and only then revokes.

steps.action: X at I8: DEV_E active with chain [CERT_E, CERT_C]
Without re-certification the revocation would suspend DEV_E itself: the pre-check refuses it
BOB re-certifies DEV_E with [CERT_E2]
DEV_E revokes DEV_C and stays active
DEV_E retires itself; rotation is left to another installation

assertions: A device never re-certifies itself (device_grant_self_recertify_active_managing).

cases.description: Rotating I while PAIR_J and PAIR_K are open, then closing J; the rotator test on concrete states

rule.text: The new DEK is sealed to every Principal with holds(P, 1) at the new head, open pairing devices included; consumed or cancelled ones receive nothing.

steps.action: I at P2: PAIR_J open
PAIR_K open
DEV_A rotates I to epoch 1
The new DEK to OWNER
The new DEK to PAIR_J
The new DEK to PAIR_K
J's session is cancelled
A cancelled pairing device receives nothing
K's request continues in epoch 1
The rotator test of §8.1 in X (CAROL is a foreign reader) and in I

assertions: 7 without 6 in a Resource with a foreign reader, or 6 without 7: awaiting rotation, no KEY_EPOCH committed; both, or 7 alone in I where every reader is of the root: rotates.

cases.description: Crash and concurrency around every ACK of a pairing approval (I) and of revoke plus rotate (X)

rule.text: Phases are classified against the accepted chain by the table of §9.2; a phase is repeated only with its exact bytes; a KEY_EPOCH is rebuilt, never re-proposed.

steps.action: Approval journal before phase 1: the complete certificate payload of DEV_B and its digest, and the exact bytes of P3; the chain is at P2
Crash after sending P3; after restart the chain holds P3
Its ACK was lost: the exact bytes of P3 are re-sent
Phase 2 after the restart: the certificate is signed from the journaled payload (CERT_B, whose payload digest is the approval)
Crash after the ACK of P4 and before it was persisted
Exact-byte retry of P4
Revoke journal in X: revoke (OWNER, DEV_A) with reason 1; the chain is at I8
After the ACK of I9 (or after a crash), the revoke phase
The rotate phase after the revocation at I9
A rotation planned at I8 had sealed its DEK to DEV_A, a reader at I8 and not at I9, the head the KEY_EPOCH is committed on: that DEK is not used
The KEY_EPOCH with a fresh DEK is committed on I9
Partial delivery: the package of epoch 1 to BOB is sent and recorded, then the rotator crashes
After the restart the package phases are classified by the ledger: BOB complete, CAROL pending; the package to CAROL is sent
DEV_B, suspended at K1, is not a reader and is skipped
Alternative: the rotator of K1 crashed before any package; readers hold epoch 1 in KEY_BLOCKED
After a bounded wait a second rotator commits epoch 2 with a fresh DEK

assertions: No installation reconstructs a DEK it does not hold; journals hold no secrets (§9.8): the certificate payload is not a secret.

cases.description: An issuer of the planned chain is revoked between planning and resuming: a first registration and a re-certification are superseded

rule.text: (R, D) revoked, or an issuer of c's chain revoked: superseded; the issuers are those of the planned chain c, not of the current binding.

steps.action: X at I8: a first registration of DEV_M2 with [CERT_M2, CERT_A] is planned (DEV_M2 is not bound in X)
… and a re-certification of DEV_B with [CERT_B', CERT_A] (DEV_B's current leaf is CERT_B)
Before either operation resumes, OWNER revokes DEV_A, the issuer in both planned chains
The first registration resumes: superseded, nothing is signed or proposed
The re-certification resumes: superseded, nothing is signed or proposed
Control: a re-certification of DEV_B by the root with [CERT_B2], which avoids DEV_A, is pending on I9
… and committed-own once I10 is accepted

assertions: A phase is classified on the chain it would commit; the current binding of the device does not name the issuers of a chain not yet committed.

cases.description: The final frontier comes from the rotator's verified accepted set, extra ranges included

rule.text: A Have Vector is a fetch hint; a sequence the rotator could not fetch and verify stays outside the frontier; an accepted range after a hole is kept as an extra range.

steps.action: DEV_A sequence 1 in Y
DEV_A sequence 2
DEV_A sequence 4, previous = sequence 2 (sequence 3 never written)
An advertised unit that fails authorization (BRIDGE in Y) is not counted
The server advertises DEV_A 1..100; only 1, 2 and 4 are fetchable and verify
A frontier that writes the range after the hole as [3, 4] is not canonical
DEV_A closes epoch 0 with the frontier {0: DEV_A, 1: 2, 2: [[4, 4]]}
Sequence 4 received after the KEY_EPOCH: inside the extra range
A sequence 3 arriving after the KEY_EPOCH: in the hole
Sequence 5 after the KEY_EPOCH: beyond the frontier

final.frontier_rule: the verified accepted sequences of each actor: the contiguous prefix plus every accepted range after a hole (W §28.1 extra ranges)

assertions: A replica that merged sequence 4 keeps it when it learns the KEY_EPOCH; only units outside the recorded frontier are rebuilt out.

cases.description: Rotation follows exposing revocations only (independent cases, one per kind of revocation)

rule.text: A revocation that removes no registered reader never triggers a rotation; one rotation covers every exposing revocation since the last.

steps.action: An exposing revocation
An unbound tombstone without descendants
An out-of-scope binding revoked
An already suspended device revoked
A never-reading device revoked
An intermediate-only device with a reading descendant revoked
Three exposing revocations in one epoch
A former member cannot issue the tombstone at all

assertions: Exposure is computed from the Resource's own chain alone.

cases.description: Two valid competing DEVICE_GRANTs on one prev

rule.text: Neither is the head; approval and reconciliation are suspended; no branch is chosen by time, order or ACK.

steps.action: X at I1
Rd1 on I1, delivered to one manager
W1 on I1, delivered to another manager
Both branches known
Approval, reconciliation and automatic rotation taking I or X as input

assertions: A validator given both records reports CONTROL_CONFLICT and applies neither.

rule.text: Access refused alone, or revocation proven through the Control read for a revoked reader; uploads are checked by object.

DEV_A requests data
DEV_A re-supplies a valid foreign Key Package the server lost
A device that never read (DEV_W at W2)
Online: pushes stop before the revoking record is pushed (W §69)

cases.description: The four barrier entries against a pre-identity validator, a herald and an identity-aware one (independent cases)

rule.text: A pre-identity client rejects the barrier and blocks the Resource; a herald persists the blocked state with the update message; an identity-aware client accepts.

steps.action: type 9
type 10

commit field 2
A blocked client writes on its last validated head

assertions: A server whose READY lacks identity-01 rejects these records as a pre-identity receiver does.

cases.description: Devices that never received their first packages get every epoch from the next reconciling manager (independent cases)

rule.text: Key delivery is unconditional: no complaint, no data/write and no DEK of I is needed on the recipient side.

steps.action: A Read device in X
A device registered in I whose approver crashed before its first package
A service device bound in I and registered in X
None of them wrote missing_keys
